dedupe_keys.name: rerunning historical transmission outage data to value resilience investments asset hardening and faster restoration

description: This record describes a method, set out in a January 2025 author preprint from Iowa State University and co-authors, for valuing resilience investments by rerunning historical transmission outage events. Transmission utilities routinely collect detailed outage data, including resilience events in which outages bunch because of weather, and the events and their metrics can be extracted from that data. Improvements such as asset hardening or restoration investments reduce outages or speed restoration, and the paper shows how to rerun the historical events with those effects to measure the resulting improvement in resilience metrics. It is demonstrated with case studies of a derecho and a hurricane and with all large events or large thunderstorms in the Midwest USA. The authors argue that rerunning experienced events avoids the difficulty of predicting future extreme events and makes the case for investment vivid. Coverage is transmission outage events in the Midwest USA. Access: the paper on arXiv, free; the abstract gives no data or code link. Caveats: results depend on the utility outage data. It suits benefit-cost studies of resilience investment, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.
